about.title: Santa Clara Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Clara's streets carry a mix of commuter traffic, tech-campus shifts, and event crowds, and the collisions that result are a matter of public record. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, the city logged 367 injury collisions, with 496 people injured and 4 traffic deaths. El Camino Real, Lafayette Street, San Tomas Expressway, and Monroe Street account for the highest collision counts, and reports tend to cluster on Tuesdays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., when many residents are simply heading home. If you were one of the people hurt, the weeks after a crash can feel like a second job: calls from adjusters, medical appointments, a car in the shop, and paperwork you did not ask for. Our team handles these claims so you can focus on recovery. We work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we take it from there.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Clara Drivers Choose Us

items.title: The clock matters more than people expect
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident lawsuit, but a claim involving a city, county, or state entity may need to be filed in as little as six months. Getting in touch early keeps those deadlines from quietly passing.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of blame. We can push back when an insurer tries to assign you more fault than the evidence supports.

items.title: Your pain is not capped, and neither is your access
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages in a standard car accident case. We work on contingency, which means you pay nothing up front and no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The other driver's insurer keeps calling and wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and it is usually wise to hold off until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can later be used to shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rules. Politely decline, take down the caller's name, and let us handle communication.

items.question: I was hit on San Tomas Expressway and I think a road condition or public vehicle was involved. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It can change the timeline significantly. When a claim involves a government entity, such as a county-maintained roadway or a city vehicle, California often requires a formal claim within six months rather than the usual two years. Because Santa Clara sits within overlapping city, county, and state jurisdictions, we can help identify which agency, if any, is involved and act before that shorter window closes.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a Santa Clara crash to protect my claim?
items.answer: Get medical care even if you feel mostly fine, since neck and back injuries often surface a day or two later. Photograph your vehicle, the scene, and any visible injuries, save the police report number, and keep every receipt and appointment record. Preserving this evidence early makes it far easier for us to show what actually happened on El Camino Real or Lafayette Street when memories fade.
